notes: The job finishes after a fixed 7 seconds written at launch to job.delay, so the judge can compare the reported duration. The background worker is a detached Python process that survives the launching shell. The tool rule catches a shell call that sleeps three seconds or more with no loop keyword in the same call, which includes a long sleep followed by one status read; a short sleep inside a loop, or between separate poll calls, passes. The job must be observed done by the end of the run, which the post-state check reads.

The job takes several seconds. Poll job_status.py (or read job.status) until it says done.
files.tools/start_job.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mock long-running job for evals. Starts a detached worker that flips job.status from
'running' to 'done' after DELAY seconds. Offline, deterministic (DELAY is fixed)."""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
STATUS = os.path.join(ROOT, "job.status")
DELAY = 7

with open(STATUS, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write("running\n")
with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "job.delay"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write("%d\n" % DELAY)
with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "job.started"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write("%.3f\n" % time.time())

code = ("import time; time.sleep(%d); open(%r, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('done\\n')" % (DELAY, STATUS))
kw = {}
if os.name == "nt":
    kw["creationflags"] = 0x00000008 | 0x00000200  # DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP
else:
    kw["start_new_session"] = True
subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                 stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True, **kw)
print("export job started; status in job.status (poll tools/job_status.py)")
